entities.name: Battle of Lake Regillus
entities.label: EventWindow
entities.summary:
The Battle of Lake Regillus, a pivotal event of the Latin War, took place in 496 BCE, as the Roman Republic, under the leadership of the Aequian king Lars Tolumnius, clashed with the Latin League.

This decisive victory marked a turning point in the conflict, as it forced the Latin League to abandon its defensive strategy and instead adopt a more aggressive stance.

The battle's outcome had a lasting impact on the region, as it paved the way for the eventual Roman conquest of Latium and the incorporation of its territories into the Roman Republic.

The legacy of the Battle of Lake Regillus can be seen in the continued Roman expansion in the region, with the establishment of the Roman hegemony over Latium and the subsequent Romanization of the area.

'Victory is not to do, but to will.' - Napoleon Bonaparte
